fields.statement: QA at 88b6eae with the built binary (go build ./cmd/rhiza), in a scratch repo with a scripted fake claude on PATH and a fake rex: rhiza session start --prompt 'do the step', then rhiza session run <id>. (1) Fake writes 'Claude AI usage limit reached|1700000000' (reset in the past) on its first launch: session run relaunched at once as 'claude --resume <same id>' with prompt 'The usage limit has reset. Continue where you left off.', exactly one start and one resume, ended 'exited with code 0'. (2) Reset 6 s ahead: the resume came 6 s after the start, i.e. it waited for the given reset. (3) 'You've hit your limit' with no reset time: session run was still waiting after 8 s (15-minute default). (4) Limit reported on every launch: 1 start + 24 resumes, then ended 'exited with code 0', status exited code 0.

QA at 88b6eae with the built binary in a scratch repo, scripted fake claude: first launch writes 'Claude AI usage limit reached|<now+4s>' and deletes its own transcript 2 s later, during the pause. rhiza session run waited ~4 s, then relaunched 'claude --session-id <same id>' (not --resume) with the first prompt 'do the step', and printed '- Warning: the transcript of session <id> is gone after the usage-limit pause: started a fresh session for the step instead of resuming'. The fresh start shows only in that printed warning: rhiza session show <id> and the session record hold nothing about it.
